chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: Joe Smith and Bobby Hackett's sound
summary: Joe Smith had a beautiful sound that reminds Dickenson of Bobby Hackett; he knew Louis behind the blues singers.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And there was another great (unintelligible) Joe Smith. He had a beautiful sound you know. Played beautiful. reminds me of him more today than any of my -- certainly has got a beautiful sound right there.

And then he plays like Louis too. And when he plays the organ, people will say Louis. His brother Hackett's got this beautiful sound. They say Joe Smith doesn't sound like that. So you can see why I'm very fond of Bobby Hackett. He's got two guys I like all wrapped in him, you know.
Well you and Bobby can work this thing somehow and --
So when you heard Louis play behind those singers -- what's his name on the record and things like that so you know who --
I think so, but I'm not sure -- I just can't recall back in those days --
I knew his friend, yeah. Do you see what I mean by knowing what you do with this thing? You can't think to talk.
